title: Ancient Trees in Serbia: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Belgrade's biggest plane has leaned on seventeen iron posts since 1881, in front of a prince's lodge. {cities} places mapped in Serbia, {trees} trees.
intro: The old trees we map in Serbia stand on market squares, in churchyards and on park lawns, and the towns grew up around them. In Belgrade's Topčider park, a plane 7.35 metres round has rested its crown on seventeen iron posts since 1881, in front of the lodge of Prince Miloš Obrenović. A popular story says he planted it, though the city dates it to 1834 and he left for exile in 1839. Across the city, a pedunculate oak on the Cvetni trg market square is what remains of the woodland Vračar was cleared from, and a plane on Makenzijeva shades a kafana opened beside it around 1890. Two yews, one male, one female, flank Belgrade Cathedral's gate. Up the Danube in Sremski Karlovci, a plane in the Lower Church courtyard tops 30 metres. Near Niš, a reader sent us an oak at Jelašnica, 300 years old by their estimate.
